title: Legacy-row terminal fallback uses updated_at — the exact column the migration documents as polluted by takeovers
evidence:
supabase/migrations/20260813120000_reference_call_timeline_columns.sql:6-12:
"  --   terminal writer (complete_reference_call, terminalize_reference_call,
  --   sweep_terminal, exhaust_reference_call, sweep_mark_failed). `updated_at`
  --   is polluted by later writes (a takeover on an unreachable row bumps it),
  --   and `submitted_at`/`objected_at` only cover two of the seven terminal
  --   statuses — the timeline's \"Closed — no reply\"-style terminal entry needs
  --   a first-class timestamp. The detail read falls back
  --   `terminalized_at → submitted_at → objected_at → updated_at` for rows
  --   terminalized before this migration."

server/src/application/application_detail_handler.gleam:1457-1463:
"        first_non_empty([
          normalize_at(terminalized_at),
          normalize_at(submitted_at),
          normalize_at(objected_at),
          normalize_at(updated_at),
        ])"

server/src/reference_checks/sql/take_over_reference_call.sql:20-22:
"SET taken_over_at = now(),
    next_attempt_at = NULL,
    updated_at = now()"
detail: For legacy `unreachable` rows (no `terminalized_at`), a later takeover bumps `updated_at`, so the fallback stamps the terminal event AT the takeover instant — the migration's own comment identifies `updated_at` as polluted by exactly this write. Wrong evidence timestamp, colliding with the taken_over entry.
recommended_fix: When `taken_over_at` is present, skip the `updated_at` fallback (prefer `objected_at`/`submitted_at`, or no terminal event); never timestamp the terminal entry from a post-terminal write.
